questions.prompt: Put the four DHCP (DORA) messages in order.
questions.explanation: The DHCP exchange is Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge — the client discovers, a server offers, the client requests, and the server acknowledges.
DHCP runs over UDP with the server on port 67 and the client on port 68.

questions.prompt: A device has the address 169.254.10.5 and cannot reach the internet. What most likely happened?

options.text: No DHCP server responded, so it self-assigned a link-local (APIPA) address
It received a normal public address
Its DNS server is misconfigured but DHCP worked

questions.explanation: 169.254.0.0/16 is the link-local (APIPA) range used when DHCP fails; such addresses have no gateway and cannot route to the internet.

questions.prompt: What does a DHCP lease typically provide? Select all that apply.

options.text: An IP address and subnet mask

questions.explanation: DHCP delivers the address, mask, gateway, DNS servers, and a lease time. TLS certificates have nothing to do with DHCP.

questions.prompt: A DHCP address is granted for a limited time called a ____, which the client renews before it expires.
questions.explanation: A lease is a time-limited assignment; the client renews it (typically around 50% of the lease time) to keep the address.

questions.prompt: Match each DHCP term to its meaning.

pairs.right: Client broadcasts asking for a server
Server proposes an address and settings
Maps a MAC to a fixed address via DHCP
How long the address stays valid

questions.explanation: Discover asks for servers, Offer proposes config, a reservation fixes an address by MAC, and lease time bounds validity.
